p: Hounslow sits right under the Heathrow flight path, and for plane-mad kids that's half the fun. Watching the jets drift in low over the rooftops never gets old, and there are a few spots around the borough where you can see them come and go.

The High Street Quarter, where Flip Out lives, is a modern development in the town centre with a cinema and restaurants alongside, so it's easy to make a proper afternoon or evening of it without moving the car.

Beyond Osterley and Hounslow Heath, there's lots more green space to explore. Bedfont Lakes Country Park, out towards Feltham, has lakes, meadows and wildlife, and Hounslow Urban Farm in Feltham is a big community farm with rare-breed animals that younger children adore.

Over in Chiswick and Brentford, on the eastern side of the borough, Gunnersbury Park is a huge park with a free museum in a grand old mansion, plus sports facilities and a boating lake. Crane Park, near Twickenham, follows the River Crane, with a historic Shot Tower and a little island nature reserve.

Rugby fans will know that Twickenham Stadium is only a short trip away, and the stadium hosts big matches through the year. On those days, expect the roads and trains in this corner of London to be packed.
For more relaxed afternoons, Hounslow's mix of cuisines means there's no shortage of good food nearby, so you can treat the family after your session without going far.
Whether you come by Tube on the Piccadilly line or drive in from the M4, Hounslow is a handy spot for families across west London and the Thames Valley.
